summary: Scoped review of firestore.rules, not certification of the whole application. Owner-only reads, server-controlled volunteer approval and deny-all client writes prevent the tested cross-user/update bypasses. Admin SDK authorization and operational readiness are separate gates. Emulator integration covered unauthorized reads/writes, assignment, revocation and closure. No Rules changes made in this session.

findings.issue: Allowed owner collection reads do not enforce a query limit. An owner can repeatedly read their own history outside the app UI; API request budgets do not cover direct Firestore SDK reads.
findings.recommendation: Before a public launch, assess bounded list rules, App Check enforcement, quota monitoring and incident response without breaking owner document reads. A query limit alone does not prevent repeated reads. No untested enforcement was enabled.

checklist.create_update_bypass: All direct client writes, including delete and field injection, denied; tested on Emulator.
checklist.authority_source: UID from authenticated request; approval stored in server-written volunteer document. A UI purpose does not grant approval/admin.
checklist.business_logic: Private incident data via assigned/approved callable only, owner projections via SDK; multi-account and closure tests pass.
checklist.type_and_size: Client write validators in Rules not applicable because writes are denied; callable parsers validate permitted fields and portable backend bounds JSON size.
checklist.identity_vs_field_security: Owner identity checks and default deny exist; no field-only allow rule.
checklist.admin_scope: Admin SDK bypasses Rules; endpoint checks separately tested. This score does not assess legal, medical, dependency or infrastructure risk.
